title: Real estate license CE deadline Florida: a Mac routine so you stop missing it
metaTitle: Real Estate License CE Deadline Florida: A Mac Tracking Guide
description: Track your real estate license CE deadline on Mac with Apple Reminders, Calendar and Google Sheets, plus a one-week setup plan.
targetKeyword: real estate license ce deadline florida
intro: Your real estate license CE deadline in Florida is set by the state, and a miss can cost you late fees and active status in some states. The fix is to write the exact date down, then put it in a Mac alert weeks ahead. This page shows that routine, using Texas, California and Maryland rules as worked examples, because their numbers are published and checkable.
tldr: Write the exact CE due date from your state's licensing site, not from memory.
Late costs differ. California's late salesperson renewal is $525, against $350 on time.
Set two Apple Reminders alerts per license: an early one and one close to the due date.
Check the state's own tool inside its window. In Texas, that window opens 90 days before expiration.
Lazur can set the reminder by voice and guide you through the state site, but you do the clicking.

blocks.text: This page uses Texas, California and Maryland as worked examples, because their rules can be checked against official pages. Florida's exact CE hours, due date and late penalty are not stated here. Pull them from the state's licensing board before you set any date. The tracking routine below works the same way in every state.
How much does a missed CE deadline cost a realtor?

The fee is the easiest cost to measure. The bigger cost is time and status. No study I checked counts how many agents miss CE deadlines, or what a miss costs them in hours or stress. Treat any percentage with no named source as a guess.

rows: $200 deferral fee for 60 more days, or renew inactive
Renewal fees (CE hours not checked here)
15 hours per renewal period, 45 across three
Finish 30 days before renewal to avoid a reinstatement fee (amount not stated)
blocks.caption: Figures from each state's published pages, checked 2026-11-07. Florida is left blank on purpose.

blocks.text: California shows the math. A salesperson pays $525 late instead of $350 on time. A broker pays $675 instead of $450. Late fees are easy to avoid, so plan for the due date before it passes.

Texas adds a second cost. You can renew inactive without finishing CE. TREC says you must finish the hours before you return to active status. A missed deadline can keep you off active status, not only cost you a fee.
Why do CE deadlines slip past organized agents?

Psychologists call remembering to do something later prospective memory. The WashU memory lab describes two routes. You can keep watching for the task, which uses attention on whatever you are doing. Or a cue can bring the task back on its own. A CE deadline gives you few cues. Nothing tugs at you on an ordinary Tuesday.

A WashU page cites Crovitz and Daniel (1984) as finding that at least half of everyday forgetting comes from prospective memory failures. The original was not checked here, and it did not study realtors. Use the idea as a reason to set reminders, not as a measured rate for agents.

Texas also limits when you can check. Its renewal education tool works only within 90 days of your expiration date. You cannot confirm CE status months ahead on that tool. If you wait for the tool, you may learn about a gap too late.

items: A deadline two years away feels like no task at all.
Nothing in your daily work points back to it.
You may assume your brokerage tracks it. Check, because the license is yours.

blocks.text: Find the exact deadline before you set a reminder
Start with the state, not with a blog post. Work through these steps once per license, then save what you found.

items: Open your state's real estate commission or licensing board site. For Texas, start with the TREC renewal education page.
Write down the expiration date from your license record or online account.
Note the CE hours and course types the state requires for your license.
Note what a late renewal or deferral costs, and any days you get after expiration.
Save the rule page as a PDF, with the date you checked it in the file name.

blocks.text: Two details trip people up. Maryland wants CE done 30 days before your renewal date to avoid a reinstatement fee. Course vendor blogs often lag behind rule changes. Maryland's new CE regulations took effect October 1, 2024, so an old post may be wrong. Use the state site for every number.
Fix 1: set the deadline in Apple Reminders

items: Open Reminders and create a new reminder. Title it with the task, such as Finish CE hours.
Select the reminder and click Edit Details.
Turn on Date under Date & Time, then set the due date.
Turn on Time only if you want an alert at a specific hour and minute.
Open the early reminder pop-up and pick an advance alert.
For a repeating task, open the repeat pop-up. For a custom interval, choose Custom, then Frequency.

blocks.text: Set two alerts for every license. The first lands while you still have room to finish the hours. The second lands close to the due date. Maryland's 30-day rule is a good model for the early one. Paste the rule page link into the reminder, so the source is one click away.
Fix 2: mirror the deadline in Calendar

Calendar gives you a second place to see the same deadline. Click Create Quick Event in the toolbar, then choose New Reminder. Set the date next to remind me, and pick a Reminders list or leave the default. Turn on the Scheduled Reminders checkbox in the calendar list to see them there. Deleted items go to Recently Deleted in Reminders, so a mistake can be undone.
Fix 3: keep one CE tracker in Google Sheets
A sheet holds more than one license and more than one deadline. Make one row per license. The columns below hold the facts you need at a glance.

rows: The state that issued the license
Expiration date from your license record
Hours and course types from the state's rule page
Hours completed so far, updated after each course
A formula: CE needed minus CE done
Link to the rule page and the date you read it
blocks.caption: One row per license. Keep it short enough to read on screen.

blocks.text: Add a column that says whether the Reminders alert is set. A plain yes or no catches the gap a missing alert leaves. For the sheet setup, see /for/realtors/google-sheets. Save each certificate to one folder, and link it in the row.
Fix 4: check the state tool before its window closes

Each state has its own window for checking. The Texas tool works only within 90 days of expiration, so put a Calendar item on the day that window opens. For Maryland, put an item 30 days before renewal, the date the CE must be finished.

Ask for confirmation in writing. Write to your state board or broker and ask them to confirm the due date and the late cost. Use Gmail for the request, and save the reply in the license folder. For a faster inbox routine, see /for/realtors/gmail.
Common mistakes that cost realtors time

items: Setting one alert on the due date. A same-day alert leaves no time to finish.
Trusting an old post for hours or fees. Maryland's new CE regulations took effect October 1, 2024.
Thinking an inactive renewal finishes the job. In Texas, CE comes before active status.
Keeping certificates only in email. Save each one to a folder you can search.
Waiting for a state notice. Maryland warns that random CE audits can lead to disciplinary charges if you fail to comply or respond.

Spend about a week on this, one step per day. Each day adds one layer, so you can stop after any day and still be ahead of where you started.

faq.question: What is the real estate license CE deadline in Florida?
faq.answer: This page does not state Florida's due date, required hours or late penalty, because those rules were not verified in the sources used here. Check the state licensing board's official page, then write the date into Apple Reminders with an early alert.

faq.question: How many CE hours do Texas real estate agents need?
faq.answer: TREC says license holders must complete 18 hours of continuing education during each two-year license period. Brokers must also complete a six-hour Broker Responsibility Course within those 18 hours.

faq.question: What happens if I miss my CE deadline in Texas?
faq.answer: You can pay a $200 CE deferral fee, which gives you 60 more days from the expiration date to finish. You can also renew inactive. Inactive renewal does not require CE, but you must complete it before returning to active status.

faq.question: How do I set a CE reminder on Mac?
faq.answer: Open Reminders, create the item, and click Edit Details. Turn on Date under Date & Time, then use the early reminder pop-up for an advance alert. Use the repeat pop-up for recurring reminders.

faq.question: Is the Texas renewal tool a way to check CE months ahead?
faq.answer: No. TREC's renewal education tool is available only to agents and brokers within 90 days of their expiration date. Mark a Calendar item for the day the window opens.

faq.question: What is the Maryland CE deadline rule?
faq.answer: Maryland says CE courses must be completed 30 days before the license renewal date to avoid a reinstatement fee. The page does not state the fee amount. Maryland requires 15 hours per renewal period, or 45 across three periods.

faq.question: Can Lazur track my CE deadlines for me?
faq.answer: Lazur can set dated Apple Reminders and Calendar events by voice, and it can guide you through a state site one click at a time. It does not click buttons or operate the state site for you, and you still check the official rule.

faq.question: Is my information safe if I use Lazur for this?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots are sent to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Keep client personal details out of your CE notes, and follow your brokerage rules on client data.

costs.title: Late renewal fees
costs.text: California shows how fast late renewal costs add up. A salesperson pays $525 late instead of $350 on time. A broker pays $675 instead of $450. These are the state's own fees, and they are easy to avoid with a dated reminder.

costs.title: A deferral fee that buys time
costs.text: Texas lets you pay a $200 CE deferral fee when you renew without finished CE. The deferral gives you 60 more days from the expiration date to finish. That is time, bought at a price. It does not waive the hours.

costs.title: Active status on hold
costs.text: Renewing inactive in Texas avoids finishing CE for that renewal. But TREC says you must complete the hours before you return to active status. Time spent inactive is time away from active status, and you can plan around it only if you know the date.

costs.title: Maryland reinstatement and audit risk
costs.text: Maryland wants CE finished 30 days before renewal to avoid a reinstatement fee. The page does not state that fee. Maryland also warns that random CE audits may lead to disciplinary charges if you fail to comply or respond.

costs.title: Hours spent hunting for dates
costs.text: Without one list, you rebuild the due date each time someone asks. You search old emails, portal screens and certificates. The state rule and your own records may also disagree, so you spend time working out which one is right.

causes.title: Future tasks have no built-in cue
causes.text: Remembering a task for later works in two ways, according to the WashU memory lab. You can keep watching for it, which costs attention. Or a cue can trigger it. A CE deadline gives you few cues, so it depends on your watching.

causes.title: The deadline sits two years away
causes.text: Texas counts CE per two-year license period, so the due date can feel far off for most of that time. A task that is far away gets pushed behind this week's showings and calls. The date then arrives with little warning.

causes.title: The state check tool opens late
causes.text: In Texas, the renewal education tool is available only within 90 days of your expiration date. You cannot see your CE status months ahead on that tool. Many agents look near the end of the window, when there is little time left to finish hours.

causes.title: Someone else seems to own it
causes.text: You may assume your brokerage tracks CE, or that the course provider will remind you. The license belongs to you. Provider reminders and brokerage systems vary, so check your own record.

causes.title: Course proof lives in too many places
causes.text: Certificates often sit in a provider's account or an old email. At renewal time, you search for proof of completion. Saving each certificate to one folder when you finish stops that search.

fixes.title: Write the exact date from the state site
fixes.text: Start with the state's own rule page. Copy the expiration date, the required hours and the late cost into a note with today's date. A date taken from memory or a forum post is an easy way to miss one.

fixes.title: Set a dated Apple Reminders alert with an early warning
fixes.text: Open Reminders, create the item, and click Edit Details. Turn on Date under Date & Time, then use the early reminder pop-up for an advance alert. Pick an early date you can act on, not only the due date itself.

fixes.title: Mirror the deadline in Calendar
fixes.text: Calendar can show your reminders in the same view as meetings and showings. Click Create Quick Event in the toolbar, choose New Reminder, and set the date next to remind me. Turn on Scheduled Reminders to see it in the calendar list.

fixes.title: Keep one CE tracker in Google Sheets
fixes.text: One sheet with one row per license shows what is due, what is done and what is left. A plain yes or no column for the alert catches gaps. The sheet needs only the state's numbers and your course records, and nothing else.

fixes.title: Check the state tool before its window closes
fixes.text: If your state has a window for checking CE status, put the day that window opens on your calendar. In Texas, the tool opens 90 days before expiration. Use that day to confirm your hours, not the final week.

fixes.title: Get the rule in writing from the state or your broker
fixes.text: Email the state board or your broker and ask them to confirm the due date, the hours and the late cost. Keep the reply with the saved rule page. A written answer is easier to show later than a memory of a phone call.

plan.text: Open your state's licensing site. Write down the expiration date, the CE hours and the late cost. Save the rule page with the date you checked it.
